label: shape-B
summary: The network's predicted risk is a sigmoid of a linear score (heart rate, age, creatinine, smoking, diabetes and male sex raise it) plus four hinged parts. Its main nonlinear effect is a saddle in systolic pressure and heart rate: a pressure-over-rate hinge raises risk when systolic pressure is high for the heart rate, a serial chain of hinges on pressure plus rate pulls risk down when both are high, so at systolic 110 mmHg risk rises with heart rate from 3% to 90% while at systolic 150 it falls. Bmi acts through an amplifier that is flat at low bmi and rising above a turn; age rises linearly and then flattens in the early eighties through an age-ceiling hinge; sodium and noise are not connected. The annotated model reproduces the network to 4.4e-16 on the 1500 training rows, and linearising every hidden unit lowers training AUC from 0.8458 to 0.7450.

leaves.name: age_ceiling
leaves.why: A single age hinge that switches on in the early eighties and cancels the direct age term, so the model's risk stops rising with age; age alone predicts it.

leaves.name: pressure_rate_load
leaves.why: A serial chain of hinges on systolic pressure plus heart rate that lowers risk ever more steeply when both are high (rate-pressure product also reads it well).

leaves.name: pressure_over_rate
leaves.why: A hinge on systolic pressure high relative to heart rate that raises risk steeply; the pressure-minus-rate difference predicts it almost perfectly.

leaves.name: rate_bmi_amplifier
leaves.why: Two near-linear hinges carrying the bmi effect (flat then rising) and part of the heart-rate effect; graded meaningful by the probe but read as a general haemodynamic-plus-body-size load rather than one clinical concept.

leaves.name: direct_terms
leaves.why: The linear risk score of direct edges; the probe grade is meaningful but its concept is the part's own leading terms, so it is described by its formula more than explained.

overall_function: The network adds a linear score (heart rate, age, creatinine, smoking, diabetes, male sex) to four hinged parts and passes the sum through a sigmoid. Its central effect is a saddle in systolic pressure and heart rate: risk is high when pressure is high and the heart rate slow, or when the heart rate is fast and pressure low, and falls when both are high together, so neither input is monotone on its own. Bmi acts through a hinge that is flat at low bmi and rising above a turn whose position depends on heart rate and pressure; age rises linearly and then flattens in the oldest patients through a ceiling hinge, with creatinine shifting that turn slightly. Sodium and the noise column are not connected to the output, so the model ignores them.
clinical_terms: The model gives a high predicted risk to patients with a high systolic pressure and a slow heart rate (a wide pressure-rate gap) and to patients with a fast heart rate at low or normal pressure, but a low risk when both pressure and heart rate are high together, a joint pattern that detects a mismatch between pressure and rate rather than either alone. Older age raises the risk up to the early eighties and then no further; higher creatinine, smoking, diabetes and male sex each raise it; higher bmi raises it only above a turn in the overweight range. Serum sodium has no effect on the model's prediction.
stuck: Resumed after an interruption; the only fix needed was one stale-provenance query in the root (re-run, values unchanged). The direct terms and the rate-bmi amplifier have no single clinical reading beyond their weighted sums.
